> **Update 0.2.4.1:** DeepSeek setup now works from the installed Terminal. The 0.2.4 Terminal package was missing the DeepSeek preparation scripts, so setup stopped at "Preparing your model". If you installed 0.2.4, run `strata update`, then run your DeepSeek setup again. New installs get the fix automatically. The RTX 3060 figure below is corrected to the release defaults (8 to 10 tokens/s; DSpark stays off by default on 12 GB cards).

# Strata 0.2.4: DeepSeek V4.1-Flash in the Terminal

Strata now runs DeepSeek V4.1-Flash on a PC with one 12 GB graphics card and 46 to 64 GB of RAM. The engine keeps the experts it uses most in RAM and streams the rest from your SSD.

**DeepSeek is in the Terminal (`strata launch`, `strata setup`) in this release. The desktop app is unchanged (it stays 0.2.3) and gets DeepSeek in a later update.**

## What you get

- **DeepSeek V4.1-Flash** in the model list of Setup, in three sizes from [ISTA-DASLab](https://huggingface.co/ISTA-DASLab/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-GSQ-RCO-GGUF):

  | set | download | quality against the original model |
  |---|---|---|

1.1.3 lets Flash Next image chats resume from their cache, keeps rejected tool calls visible, ends the reasoning split at the model's own close token, reads checkpoints whose shards sit in a subfolder, builds on Windows again, and lets servers built from source find their structured-output library.

### Images, tool calls and reasoning

- Flash Next image chats that add another image resume from their cached prompt instead of processing it again: image streams sit in the standard frame, and positioned pooling reads the image's three position axes. Malformed image spans are refused before anything is allocated (#1200).
- With `parallel_tool_calls: false`, a call to a tool the request did not offer, or a malformed call, comes back as text in `content` instead of being dropped, and it does not use up the one allowed call (#1207).
- The reasoning split ends at the model's own close token, so a `</think>` that the reply quotes as text no longer ends `reasoning_content` early (#1180).

# Penny Royal 3.1.2

This patch release gives the maintained native-MTP profiles one public
width-policy setting, fixes DFlash2 decode-checkpoint tracking, stops the
scheduler's idle sleep from delaying encoder-embedding handoffs, and labels
both DFlash2 profiles experimental / alpha. Model, profile and performance
defaults are unchanged from 3.1.1: the `tiered` width routing still launches
exactly what it launched before.

## Published image

Image: `ghcr.io/jpezzulli/sglang-rtxpro6000:v3.1.2`

Digest: `sha256:013a685d042b178842cbf016e7deb8d23113b87044355ef785dbee6d56e57db6`

The image was built from [`fe35e1d817`](https://github.com/jpezzulli/sglang-rtxpro6000/commit/fe35e1d817d1875c57d0cfa54c950427104b4d31) and promoted after checking, without rebuilding. The release tag also includes final publication documentation.

## Fixes and changes

- **One width-policy setting.** The native-MTP launch recipes hard-coded one
  policy file and a checksum that refused anything else, so returning to the
  3.0.2 acceptance-adaptive widths meant editing launch lines. `PENNY_MTP_POLICY`
  is now the single setting that selects both the bundled policy file and the
  launch width that can carry i
